text:
Elena (CEO): Quick weekly check-in — top lines and three small asks for next week. TL;DR: 1) Private beta GA readiness is still on track but needs a final canary pass; 2) cost per 1k tokens generation down ~12% week-over-week (nice work on quant/packing); 3) p95 latency for hosted API is 210ms (target 200ms) — we need a short latency push. Also updating two product policies (see below). Calendar: 30m all-hands sync Friday 11:00am PT (invite sent). Details follow.

OpsBot: Calendar event created: "Exec weekly — priorities & canary gating" Friday 11:00am PT — 30m.

Marco (VP Product): Noted. Product will require canary gating on three metrics before GA: p95 < 190ms, error rate < 0.5% over a 10m window, and no model-quality regressions on the canonical eval set. We'll hold public GA announcement until those gates are green. Pausing external promos until legal signs off. :white_check_mark:

Priya (VP Eng): Thanks — Eng plan: 1) infra spike today to try microbatch tuning + kernel fusion experiment, 2) rolling canary will run on 10% traffic for 2 hours, 3) will enable KV-prefix caching for recurrent requests in the canary. ETA for canary metrics: EOD Thursday. Need SRE to confirm monitoring playbook.

Sam (Head SRE): SRE will own the canary playbook and run the 2-hour canary. A couple asks: raise alert threshold for host CPU from 85->90% during canary, and add a short-term alert for cache-hit-rate drop (threshold 70%). I will also add runbook links to the canary doc.

Tess (Head of Sales): Sales will freeze any GA-related promotions until we have a clear go. Also need final SLA wording (response times, incident credits) for enterprise pilots — legal, can you prioritize?

LegalBot: Draft SLA language queued. We'll provide a tidy paragraph + a short redlines list by EOD Thursday.

Elena (CEO): Policy updates (effective immediately for self-serve accounts): 1) default data retention setting changed to 30 days (customers can opt to extend via contract for dedicated/private), 2) Private early access customers require completed SOC2 questionnaire and a security review, 3) support escalation: for Sev2/Sev1 incidents, Response Lead must be engaged within 30 minutes. These are internal defaults — PM/Support, please bake into docs.

Priya (VP Eng): Noted on retention. We need to update telemetry pipelines for the shorter retention window (data deletion job schedule). I'll assign an engineer to make the config change and run a small dry-run.

Marco (VP Product): I'll update the docs and the self-serve UI copy to reflect the 30-day default and the opt-out path for enterprise.

Sam (Head SRE): For the 30-minute response ask, SRE will adjust on-call rotations and ensure the incident page has the new SLAs.

Elena (CEO): A few metrics to watch this week: 1) Hosted p95 latency (goal <=200ms), 2) Cost per 1k tokens (target -15% month-over-month), 3) Canaries: pass rate and any quality regressions on eval set. Weekly ask: owners, please put a one-line status in #eng-status by 9am PT Thursday.

Tess (Head of Sales): Copy — Sales will provide a customer-facing FAQ draft by Thursday noon for any prospects asking about GA timing and retention defaults.

Priya (VP Eng): Quick Q: do we want to run the canary on a single region first (us-west-2) or spread across two regions? My vote: start single region, validate metrics, then roll to multi-region.

Elena (CEO): Start single region, Priya. If canary metrics look stable, do a controlled multi-region sweep.

Marco (VP Product): Will do. Adding a final ask: if any team foresees a blocker for Friday's sync, ping me directly today so we can surface it earlier.

Elena (CEO): Thanks team. Small, focused week — prioritize canary quality gates and the latency spike. :rocket:

Priya (VP Eng): :thumbsup:

Sam (Head SRE): :thumbsup: will post the canary playbook link when ready.

Elena (CEO): Closing note — great cross-team coordination last week on cost optimizations. Keep that momentum.
